newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan current account surplus on downtrend--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan current account surplus on downtrend--MOF.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, continues to be on a downward trend, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Wednesday.
"The current account surplus is in a declining trend," the MOF official told reporters.
The surplus in Japan's current account shrank 28.9 percent to 460.60 billion yen in August from a year earlier.
"The increase in imports has been outpacing increases in exports, and the deficit in services trade has been showing an upward trend," the official said.

The official also said the huge increase in the portfolio investment deficit for August indicates Japanese financial institutions are shifting capital overseas, a trend which earlier in the year was dominated by private investors.
Portfolio investment for August showed a net deficit of 1.082 trillion yen, compared to a deficit of around 127 billion yen the previous month.
